activities.name: Essays/LORs/Other: Essay was about a superstition my mom used to tell me when I
activities.description: Essays/LORs/Other: Essay was about a superstition my mom used to tell me when I was little and used it as a metaphor for learning to accept I was a late bloomer/was falling behind in knowing what I wanted. About my transition away from wanting to go to art school and following a new passion that I’m inexperienced in but still want to learn. My LORs are very strong, coming from my art teacher who is like my best friend, and my CS teacher who absolutely glazes me and my ability to learn and write code. I was also a teaching assistant (actual thing in my school) for both of their classes at one point whether official or not.

activities.name: hey, did you ever take a language class in high school? I’m an immigrant from a
activities.description: hey, did you ever take a language class in high school? I’m an immigrant from a south east asian country who moved to the US in 8th grade and was learning english as a 2nd language at the time. Now I’m a junior and just realized that I should have taken a language class. How was your process of applying if you did not take a language? If you did, any advice for me regarding applying for universities that required a language course?

activities.name: Final Thoughts: i’m actually flabbergasted that i got in, let alone to boston. i
activities.description: Final Thoughts: i’m actually flabbergasted that i got in, let alone to boston. i thought going ed1 was silly and that i’d 100% get rejected with how lackluster my application felt compared to people in my grade or people online. and i know some people will look at my ECs and say i was doing more than enough — but before my acceptance it truly didn’t feel like it. so if you’re applying to a school and you think you won’t get in in a million years, take a second and step out of all this college stuff. if you worked hard, followed your passions, and built a story of growth through your app, you have a good chance. of course not everyone can get in, but that’s okay. where you go doesn’t define you, it’s what YOU do with that learning and how YOU push your life forward. i promise you’ll find where you belong, remember to make the most of it
